title: Are fraud disputes even arbitrable - the current legal position
p1:
Can a fraud allegation take a dispute straight out of arbitration?

Many people assume that the moment someone says “fraud”, courts must decide the matter. But the legal position is more nuanced than that.
p2:
The surprising part: fraud disputes are not automatically non-arbitrable. Indian courts have moved away from the older view that every fraud claim belongs only before a court.

The real question is whether the alleged fraud affects the arbitration agreement itself or requires complex public investigation beyond a private dispute.
p3:
If the fraud claim is mainly between parties and can be decided by examining evidence, arbitration may still be possible. But cases involving serious allegations that impact public interest or challenge the very foundation of the agreement may require court intervention.

The practical takeaway: simply using the word “fraud” does not end the arbitration clause. The nature and impact of the allegation matter.
conclusion: Do you think fraud allegations should always be decided by courts, or should parties still be allowed to choose arbitration in suitable cases?
